summary.headline: Saatvik Q2 FY27 revenue rose 77% QoQ to Rs 9,026 million, but EBITDA margin slipped to 7.7%; Odisha 1.3 GW module plant began commercial production on 2 November 2026.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose 77% sequentially to Rs 9,026 million as module sales volume jumped to 640 MW from 334 MW, and the confirmed order book stood at 6.68 GW on 30 September 2026. EBITDA rose to Rs 696 million but its margin fell to 7.7% from 8.3% in Q1, and profit after tax improved to Rs 202 million from Rs 54 million. Leverage rose sharply during the Odisha build-out, with debt-to-equity at 1.37x against 0.99x in June 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue to about Rs 60,000 million at roughly 12% EBITDA margin, with the Odisha cell line targeted for ramp-up by December 2026.

segments.name: Module manufacturing
segments.commentary: Modules were about 96% of H1 revenue. Q2 production was 658 MW and sales 640 MW; effective capacity utilisation was 58.5% in Q2 and 47.4% in H1. Average realisation was Rs 13.49/Wp in Q2 and Rs 13.89/Wp for H1.

segments.name: Other businesses (EPC, solar pumps, transformers, inverters, encapsulants, batteries)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue was Rs 408 million in Q2 and Rs 64 million in H1 as stated on the call, with management saying non-module share rose to about 4% of revenue and targeted at about 15% within two years.

segments.name: Revenue mix by customer type
segments.commentary: Management stated C&I about 28%, utility about 52-55%, exports about 3% and retail about 12%. Domestic customers were 96.7% of Q2 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at about Rs 60,000 million with EBITDA margin of about 12% (analyst's H2 implied margin of 16-17% was not explicitly confirmed by management).
Odisha module plant: 1.3 GW commercial production started 2 November 2026; full 4 GW Odisha module capacity expected by December 2026, taking total module capacity to 8.8 GW.
Odisha 2.4 GW cell line: trial runs commenced; production ramp-up targeted December 2026; ALMM inspection for cells planned around November 2026.
Phase two: additional 3.6 GW cell capacity targeted for FY28, taking total cell capacity to 6 GW; phase three (ingot and wafer, 6 GW) targeted for FY29.
Encapsulant capacity to rise from 2 GW to 5 GW; capsules from 2 GW live to 5 GW by FY28.
Cell benefits expected to start partially in Q3 FY27 and more meaningfully in Q4 FY27; management declined to quote a margin number, saying it would be in line with cell-integrated peers.
Cell capacity utilisation targeted above 90% next year; module utilisation targeted back in the 80s next year, with FY27 described as a realignment year.
capex_capacity: Ambala: 4.8 GW module and 2 GW encapsulant capacity.
Odisha phase one (57 acres): 1.3 GW module line commissioned; remaining 2.7 GW to be added by December 2026 to reach 4 GW; 2.4 GW cell line in trial run.
Odisha phase two (27 acres): 3.6 GW cell capacity, completion targeted FY28.
Odisha phase three: 6 GW ingot and wafer capacity targeted for FY29, aligned with ALMM List-3 from June 2028.
Module utilisation: 85% last year; this year about 58% (as stated on the call), expected to improve in H2.
demand_pricing: Current indicative prices: DCR modules around Rs 13 per Wp and non-DCR around Rs 11.5-13 per Wp for delivery in FY28-29 (as stated on the call).
Confirmed order book 6.68 GW on 30 September 2026, about 110% of 6.1 GW installed module capacity; approximately 60% DCR and 40% non-DCR.

Q2 new orders 970 MW; H1 new orders 1.76 GW (as stated); recent wins include Rs 476 crore from Cram Engineering (August), Rs 1,041 crore from SECI (September), Rs 297.5 crore and Rs 190 crore domestic module orders (August/September), and Rs 100 crore from MSEDCL (October).
Management said the industry is moving to cell-led competition; domestic cell capacity is about 37 GW versus over 200 GW of module capacity.
India added about 20.8 GW of solar in H1 FY27; management expects demand of about 50 GW in FY27 rising to 85 GW by FY30.
US Section 232 tariffs on polysilicon-based products from 4 December; exports are about 3% of revenue.
China technology export controls: management said it is monitoring and sees limited impact on the Odisha phase two equipment, with alternatives available in Germany.

qa_highlights.question: What are the module price realisations for DCR and non-DCR segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management indicated about Rs 13/Wp for DCR and about Rs 11.5-13/Wp for non-DCR, for delivery in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Does the China export control on technology transfer affect phase two cell capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is watching developments; phase two equipment tie-up is in place and it should not delay cell equipment, with alternative sources in Germany.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Surya Connect solar kit's business model and competitive position?
qa_highlights.answer: Kits are sold as turnkey projects via distributors and online, installed by local empanelled installers; about 85-90 B2C reseller and distributor partners, with expansion underway.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy for EPC and other non-module businesses, and what share do they target?
qa_highlights.answer: Aim is to lift share of project value from about 50-60% (modules) to 70-80% by integrating inverters and transformers; non-module share of revenue is about 4% in H1 and targeted at about 15% within two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 and FY28 revenue and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue guided at about Rs 60,000 million with about 12% EBITDA margin; H2 EBITDA expected to improve with Odisha. FY28 specifics not given beyond cell utilisation targets above 90% and module utilisation back in the 80s.

qa_highlights.question: What margin benefit does backward integration bring and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Benefits start partially in Q3 FY27 and more in Q4 FY27; margin to be in line with cell-integrated peers, with no explicit number given.

qa_highlights.question: How is vapour (wafer input) and encapsulant supply secured for Odisha cells?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term contracts with tier-one Chinese suppliers; vapour purchases already made for ongoing cell production; encapsulant capacity to rise from 2 GW to 5 GW.

risks_watch: Balance sheet: debt-to-equity rose to 1.37x from 0.99x in June 2026 as Odisha is built; management says it will manage leverage with discipline.
Execution: Odisha module ramp to 4 GW by December 2026, cell ramp by December 2026, and ALMM List-2 inspection timing (management said within November 2026) are the key milestones.
Policy: ALMM List-2 (cells) enforced from 1 June 2026 with no blanket extension; exemption only for net-metering and open-access projects commissioned by 31 December 2026; ALMM List-3 from June 2028.
Margin pressure: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 7.7%; FY27 guidance of about 12% requires H2 margin recovery.
Working capital: inventory and receivables increased sharply, with stock built ahead of Odisha execution.
China technology export controls expected around 15 November; impact on phase two equipment still being assessed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on project milestones and the integration strategy, but cautious on margins and leverage, with the CFO acknowledging that leverage has risen during the build phase. Management declined to quantify cell margins and utilisation for FY28, describing FY27 as a realignment year.
key_quotes: The approach remains to build a business with healthy economics and long term value creation rather than to pursue volume at any cost.
We are conscious that leverage has risen during the build phase.
In margins we cannot give a number but it will be in line with our peers who are already in cell manufacturing.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at about Rs 60,000 million (≈Rs 6,000 crore) with ~12% EBITDA margin, but H1 revenue was Rs 14,136 million and H1 margin 7.9%, so the H2 implied step-up depends on the Odisha 4 GW module and 2.4 GW cell lines ramping by December 2026, backed by a 6.68 GW order book (~110% of installed module capacity) and 970 MW Q2 orders.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 7.7% from 8.3% in Q1, but management guides FY27 to about 12%, implying H2 recovery as cell benefits start partially in Q3 and more meaningfully in Q4 FY27 (H1 margin only 7.9%).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Odisha 1.3 GW module line began commercial production on 2 Nov 2026, with the remaining 2.7 GW to reach 4 GW by December 2026 and the 2.4 GW cell line in trial runs with ramp-up targeted December 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 module sales rose to 640 MW from 334 MW and the confirmed order book is 6.68 GW (about 110% of 6.1 GW installed module capacity), though module utilisation was only 58.5% in Q2 and 47.4% in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Phase two 3.6 GW cell capacity (FY28) and phase three 6 GW ingot and wafer (FY29) are already planned, and management described the cell capacity target of above 90% utilisation, so further capex decisions are probable though not yet announced beyond these.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of about Rs 60,000 million was only held, and H1 revenue was Rs 14,136 million, so the H2 step-up required (about Rs 45,864 million) leaves little room for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin was 7.9% against the about 12% FY27 guide, the H2 step-up depends on the Odisha 4 GW module and 2.4 GW cell ramps by December 2026, and the China technology export controls around 15 November are still being assessed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Cell manufacturing (2.4 GW Odisha line, ramp targeted December 2026) and encapsulant expansion from 2 GW to 5 GW by FY28 are new product lines, with non-module share of revenue targeted at about 15% within two years from about 4% today.

rows.label: ALMM List-2 cell inspection and compliance
rows.why: ALMM inspection for cells is planned around November 2026 and ALMM List-2 is enforced from 1 June 2026 with no blanket extension, so Odisha cell timing ties directly to DCR cell demand (DCR modules about Rs 13/Wp, about 60% of order book).

rows.label: Inventory and receivables build-up
rows.why: Inventory rose to Rs 9,074 million from Rs 7,016 million in March 2026 and receivables to Rs 4,855 million from Rs 688 million, while debt-to-equity rose to 1.37x from 0.99x in June 2026, so cash conversion must improve for leverage to ease.

rows.label: Order book conversion
rows.why: Confirmed order book of 6.68 GW on 30 September 2026 (about 110% of installed module capacity) with Q2 new orders of 970 MW and recent wins such as Rs 1,041 crore from SECI in September.

tone.note: Management was confident on Odisha milestones, order book and the backward-integration strategy, but cautious on the Q2 margin dip, rising leverage (debt-to-equity 1.37x) and cell margins, which it declined to quantify; analysts pushed on H2 margin recovery to the 12% guide and on DCR/non-DCR price
